script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The cookie-swap comparison does not match Paul's action of proclaiming the testimony without eloquence or wisdom. Showing up with dough and a smile does not clarify that contrast.
The passage says Paul proclaimed the testimony about God, but it does not say that was the whole reason he came.
Saying Paul never wandered down another aisle turns his stated resolve into a claim that he addressed no other subject. Paul also says he speaks wisdom among the mature.
The passage contrasts persuasive words of wisdom with a demonstration of the Spirit's power. It does not say the Spirit's power took the place of philosophers.
Paul says the rulers of this age are coming to nothing. The explanation shifts that claim to their wisdom, saying it is on its way out.
Calling 'before time began' a long time ago turns Paul's statement into a span of time, which the text does not say.
The passage says no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined what God prepared. Saying they could not get there alone changes those statements into a claim about ability.
The claim that a person's spirit hears their thoughts first adds a sequence the passage does not give. Friends can also learn things without being told directly.
Paul does not say that the rulers' coming to nothing is why their praise is not what he seeks. The explanation supplies that connection.
Saying nobody gets to judge the spiritual man overstates Paul's wording that he is not subject to anyone's judgment.
The explanation repeats the verse and asks the baker to reread it, but does not explain the answer.
The statement that Moses was Israel's leader is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
